source.description: One reviewed six-panel graphite-and-colored-pencil contact sheet cropped into five cumulative process frames and one finished master.
source.notes: Keep one pair of vintage binoculars in a stable three-quarter view with exactly two tapered barrels, two large objective lenses, two smaller eyepieces, one central hinge, one focus wheel, one continuous leather strap, two attachment points including one visible side ring, one buckle, grip ribs, and one broken tabletop shadow.

process_strategy: Reserve both barrel axes, lens ellipses, bridge, eyepieces, focus wheel, strap loop, buckle, attachment points, and shadow in pale construction; convert those same guides into persistent contours; stop the strap behind the barrels and bridge at reserved crossings; add glass, grip, leather texture, and restrained color before limiting the final panel to keeper-line and value cleanup.

rejection_checks: Keep one pair of binoculars, one three-quarter view, one crop, and one scale in all six panels.

Keep exactly two barrels, two objective lenses, two eyepieces, one bridge, one focus wheel, one continuous strap, two attachment points, one buckle, and one shadow after those routes appear; no landmark may disappear and return.
The strap, bridge, near barrel, and far barrel must meet only at reserved overlaps; no keeper line may be erased to fake depth.
Do not add a case, hands, person, bird, landscape, logo, lettering, label, arrow, number, signature, watermark, or decorative border.
The final panel may not introduce a lens, eyepiece, hardware part, strap segment, buckle, texture cluster, shadow shape, or color area.
The finish must look like tactile graphite and colored pencil on warm paper, not glossy product art, photorealism, or rasterized vector illustration.
